name: Hancore
tagline: Personal site of Hancore, a designer and engineer in Germany, built like a code editor
description:
Hancore is the personal site of a designer and engineer who builds open-source software for the Omarchy community. The home page is a dark wall of code with a Vim-style status line. A link labeled enter opens a second view with projects, themes, a stack, and a log.

The second view names the projects Shibumi-Shell, quickshell-dots, waybar-themes, and OmaQ. The site links to the GitHub account HANCORE-linux, plus Discord, Ko-fi, and Buy Me a Coffee. It states no license for the page design. The GitHub profile places Hancore in Germany.
pricing_detail: The site is free to view. The page links to Ko-fi and Buy Me a Coffee for optional support. It states no price and no license for the site design.
agent_guidance:
Use it as a taste reference for a personal site that uses a code-editor layout. Read the site page for the project list, because the home page is mostly a canvas.

Treat the page as a reference. Do not copy the artwork or the code into another product. The linked repositories are separate open-source projects.
why_it_matters: It shows a personal portfolio that uses a code-editor layout for projects, themes, and a log.
tier_reason: A clear personal site with real projects and a code-editor layout. It grants no reuse rights, and it is one portfolio.
notable_for: themes, stack, and a log on one page
no stated license for the site design
evidence: Checked https://hancore.dev/ and https://hancore.dev/site/ in curl and Chromium on 2026-10-12. The home page is a code wall, and the site page lists Shibumi-Shell, quickshell-dots, waybar-themes, and OmaQ. The GitHub profile HANCORE-linux links back to the site. The GitHub profile listed 1279 followers on 2026-10-12. /about, /work, and /projects return 404. robots.txt explains content signals but sets none. The owner shared https://hancore.dev/ on 2026-10-12 and asked to file personal sites in their matching categories.
